newsitem.title: USA: GM reaches pact to end Ohio truck strike.
newsitem.headline: GM reaches pact to end Ohio truck strike.

text.p: General Motors Corp. said Tuesday it reached a tentative agreement with the International Union of Electronics Workers to end a three-day-old strike at its sport utility vehicle plant in Moraine, Ohio.
GM spokesman Gerald Holmes said production of Chevrolet Blazer, GMC Jimmy and Oldsmobile Bravada vehicles is scheduled to resume at the suburban Dayton, Ohio, plant early Wednesday.
"We've reached a tentative agreement to end the strike at Moraine," he said.

Holmes declined to disclose details of the new local labour agreement, but said he believed it does not contain the harsh penalties for absenteeism that caused about 4,100 members of IUE Local 801 to reject a previous local pact last week.
"That was taken out before the strike started. I can't imagine why they would put that back in," Holmes said.
The workers struck the sport utility vehicle plant on Sunday. Through Tuesday, GM has lost two full days worth of production at the factory, or about 2,000 vehicles.
GM officials said a ratification vote for the new contract will take place on Thursday and Friday.
